croatia-adriatic-dreams.lead: Croatia from the capital to the coast: Plitvice’s waterfalls, Diocletian’s Palace and a private boat through the Pakleni Islands, finishing in Dubrovnik.

reasons.t: Waterfalls and an Orient Express hotel
reasons.d: A night at the Esplanade Zagreb, built in 1925 for Orient Express passengers, then Plitvice’s sixteen interconnected emerald lakes and Croatia’s tallest waterfall at 78 metres.

reasons.t: A palace that is still a town
reasons.d: Diocletian’s Palace in Split, a 4th-century imperial retirement complex that is still a living town, and the Cathedral of Saint Domnius, the oldest in use in its original structure.
A private boat day through the Pakleni Islands off Hvar, sunset from the Fortica fortress, then Dubrovnik’s Old City, its walls and the Elaphiti Islands.

france-and-germany-paris-to-berlin.lead: Paris to Berlin by way of Alsace and Bavaria: the Louvre, half-timbered Strasbourg, Neuschwanstein and the Cold War in Berlin.

reasons.d: Three nights on Avenue Montaigne, with the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame, a private Seine dinner cruise and a private Montmartre food walk.
Strasbourg’s UNESCO-listed Grande Île and the half-timbered canals of Petite France, with an Alsatian dinner of flammekueche, choucroute, Munster and local white wine.
Munich’s Marienplatz, Glockenspiel and Viktualienmarkt, a day at Neuschwanstein, and Berlin’s history and Cold War story from the Hotel Adlon Kempinski.

france-grand-journey.lead: France end to end: a privately guided Louvre and Versailles, Loire châteaux, Lyon’s food and the Riviera from Nice to Saint-Paul-de-Vence.

reasons.d: The Louvre with its Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo and Winged Victory, Notre-Dame and the Île de la Cité, a Seine dinner cruise and a private food walk, from three nights at the Plaza Athénée.
The Hall of Mirrors, the King’s Grand Apartments and Le Nôtre’s gardens, then the Loire châteaux from Les Sources de Cheverny.
Lyon from the InterContinental Hôtel-Dieu, then Nice at the Negresco, Monaco, Èze, Cannes, Antibes and Saint-Paul-de-Vence.

greece-aegean-elegance.lead: Athens’ ancient sites, Mykonos’s windmills and Delos, then Santorini’s caldera, in ten private days.

reasons.d: The Acropolis, Parthenon and Theatre of Dionysus, the Acropolis Museum with glass floors over a live excavation, and a guided Athens food walk.
Three nights on Elia Beach at Myconian Avaton, Little Venice and the Kato Mili windmills, and Delos, birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.
Canaves Oia, with fire, sea and the caldera at your door.

greece-and-turkey-aegean-to-bosphorus.lead: Athens, Santorini’s volcano, the little-visited island of Chios and Istanbul: a journey across the Aegean that ends on two continents.

reasons.t: Ancient Athens with a private guide
reasons.d: The Acropolis, Parthenon and Acropolis Museum, and the Ancient Agora, where Socrates walked and democracy was argued into existence.
Three nights at Canaves Oia, built into the caldera wall, a private boat to Nea Kameni’s smoking crater and the hot springs of Palea Kameni, and a private Assyrtiko tasting in the volcanic vineyards.
Chios’s mastic villages and medieval castle on an island almost no visitor sees, then Istanbul from the Four Seasons at Sultanahmet.

italy-and-malta.lead: Rome and Florence for the great art, a Tuscan day, then Malta: Valletta, Mdina and Gozo.

reasons.d: The Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, and the Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St Peter’s Basilica.

reasons.t: Florence, with early entry to David
reasons.d: The Uffizi and the Accademia with early entry to David, then a Tuscan day through Siena, Chianti and San Gimignano.
Valletta, with 320 monuments in 55 hectares, St John’s Co-Cathedral and Caravaggio’s Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, then Mdina, Rabat, Gozo and Comino, staying at The Phoenicia.

italy-icons.lead: Rome, Florence, a Tuscan wine estate and Venice by gondola: Italy’s great icons, privately guided.

reasons.d: The Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill with a private guide, then the Vatican Museums, the Sistine Chapel and St Peter’s Basilica.
Michelangelo’s David at the Accademia, the Uffizi’s Botticelli, Leonardo, Raphael and Caravaggio, and Brunelleschi’s dome and the Gates of Paradise.
A private day through Siena, a Chianti wine estate and San Gimignano, then Venice from the Danieli, with a gondola and a visit to Murano and Burano.

italy-la-dolce-vita.lead: Rome with a rooftop bar and a cooking lesson, then four nights above the Amalfi Coast at Caruso and a day on Capri.

reasons.d: Three nights above the Spanish Steps at Hotel de la Ville with its Cielo rooftop bar, and a private Roman cooking lesson ending in dinner of what you have made.
Siena, a Chianti estate and San Gimignano, with a chauffeur so the wine is part of the day.
Four nights in an 11th-century palace with the coast’s most famous infinity pool, then Positano, Amalfi and a day on Capri.

netherlands-and-belgium-low-countries.lead: Amsterdam’s canal palaces, windmill villages and Rotterdam’s architecture, then Brussels, Bruges and Ghent.

reasons.d: Three nights at the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam, spread across six canal palaces on the Herengracht, plus a private canal cruise and walks through the Jordaan, the Begijnhof and the Nine Streets.
Zaanse Schans, Volendam and Marken in one countryside day, and Rotterdam’s Markthal, Cube Houses and Erasmus Bridge.
Brussels’ Grand Place, then Bruges from Hotel Dukes’ Palace, and Ghent.

netherlands-dutch-grand-experience.lead: Five nights at the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam with the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh, then tulips, Giethoorn and Kinderdijk’s windmills.

reasons.d: The Rijksmuseum’s Night Watch and Vermeer, and the Van Gogh Museum’s 200 paintings, 500 drawings and 700 letters.
A private cruise through the UNESCO-listed canal ring, working windmills, cheesemaking and a clog workshop at Zaanse Schans, and the windmills of Kinderdijk.
The Keukenhof’s tulips in season, the canal-laced village of Giethoorn, then Rotterdam, Delft and The Hague from Hotel Des Indes.

spain-and-portugal-iberian-discovery.lead: Madrid, Seville, Lisbon and Porto in ten days: the Prado, the Alcázar, flamenco, Belém and the Douro Valley.

reasons.d: The Prado privately guided, the Royal Alcázar and the climb up the Giralda, and a private flamenco performance with Andalusian cuisine.
The Four Seasons Ritz Lisbon, Belém Tower and the Jerónimos Monastery, then Sintra and the Atlantic coast.
A stay at The Yeatman in Porto and a day in the Douro Valley.

spain-grand-escape.lead: Madrid’s palaces, Seville’s Alcázar by high-speed train, Barcelona’s Gaudí and a finish on Ibiza by sea.

reasons.d: Two nights at the Mandarin Oriental Ritz, opened in 1910 at the king’s request, with the Prado privately guided and the Royal Palace and Retiro.
High-speed rail to Seville at up to 320 km/h, the Royal Alcázar’s layers of Islamic, Gothic and Mudéjar work, and a private flamenco performance.
Barcelona’s Gaudí from Hotel Arts, then Ibiza by sea, staying at Nobu Hotel Ibiza Bay.

switzerland-alpine-grand-tour.lead: Switzerland’s great set pieces in ten days: the Rhine Falls, Lucerne, Mount Pilatus, the Jungfraujoch and Zermatt.

reasons.d: Mount Pilatus by the Golden Round Trip, with a boat, the world’s steepest cogwheel railway and a cable car, and the GoldenPass panoramic train to Interlaken.
The Jungfraujoch, Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald, from the Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa, then Zermatt at Mont Cervin Palace.

The Rhine Falls, Europe’s largest waterfall, by boat, medieval Stein am Rhein, and Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge, the oldest covered wooden bridge in Europe, from Baur au Lac, in its own park on Lake Zurich since 1844.

switzerland-and-germany-alps-to-bavaria.lead: The Swiss Alps then Bavaria and Berlin: Mount Pilatus, Munich, Neuschwanstein and a Cold War day in Berlin.

reasons.d: Two nights at Baur au Lac, the Rhine Falls by boat, medieval Stein am Rhein, Lucerne’s Chapel Bridge and Lion Monument, and Mount Pilatus by the Golden Round Trip.
The Mandarin Oriental Palace puts three Michelin-starred restaurants under one roof.
Marienplatz, the Glockenspiel and the Viktualienmarkt, a day at Neuschwanstein, then Berlin’s history from the Hotel Adlon Kempinski.

turkey-empires-balloons-turquoise-coast.lead: Istanbul’s empires, a sunrise balloon over Cappadocia’s fairy chimneys, Pamukkale, Ephesus and the Turquoise Coast.

reasons.d: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque, the Hippodrome and the Basilica Cistern, Topkapı Palace, a Bosphorus dinner cruise between two continents and a street-food journey through the Spice Bazaar.
A sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the fairy chimneys, after two nights at the Museum Hotel.
Pamukkale’s travertine terraces, the ruins of Ephesus and Selçuk, and a finish on the coast at Maxx Royal Belek near Antalya.
